title: Nominalisation
description: Master nominalisation for Grade 11: turning verbs and adjectives into nouns for formal and academic writing, with bilingual notes, examples, practice and tests.

topics.title: Forming Nominalisations
topics.concept:
We turn verbs and adjectives into nouns using typical suffixes:

SuffixFrom verb/adjectiveNoun
-tion / -sioneducate / decideeducation / decision
-mentdevelop / movedevelopment / movement
-ityable / activeability / activity
-nesshappy / kindhappiness / kindness
-al / -ancearrive / acceptarrival / acceptance

The whole clause is then rebuilt around the noun: The country grew rapidly → the rapid growth of the country. The adverb ('rapidly') becomes an adjective ('rapid'), and the subject becomes a possessive or 'of'-phrase.

topics.title: Nominalisation in Academic Writing — and Its Limits
topics.concept:
Nominalisation makes writing more formal, compact and objective, which suits reports, essays and science:

  • Casual: Because pollution increased, many people fell ill.
  • Formal: The increase in pollution caused widespread illness.

It lets you make the idea the subject (the increase, the decision, the failure), creating an impersonal, authoritative tone.

But beware overuse. Too much nominalisation makes writing heavy and vague — 'zombie nouns' hide the real action:

  • Heavy: The implementation of the reduction of expenditure was a cause of the improvement of profits.
  • Clearer: Cutting spending improved profits.

Use nominalisation to sound formal and concise — not to bury the meaning.

intro.en: Nominalisation is turning a verb or adjective into a noun: decide → decision, happy → happiness. It lets us 'package' a whole idea into a single noun phrase, which is why it is the engine of formal and academic English. "The government decided" becomes "The government's decision…" — more compact, more objective, more scholarly.
intro.hi: नामीकरण (nominalisation) किसी क्रिया या विशेषण को संज्ञा में बदलना है: decide → decision, happy → happiness। यह पूरे विचार को एक संज्ञा-पदबंध में 'पैक' करने देता है, इसीलिए यह औपचारिक और शैक्षणिक अंग्रेज़ी का इंजन है। "The government decided" बन जाता है "The government's decision…" — अधिक संक्षिप्त, अधिक वस्तुनिष्ठ, अधिक विद्वत्तापूर्ण।

real_life.situation:
Compare a casual line with a report line:

Casual: They developed the software, and it improved how the company works.

Formal: The development of the software led to an improvement in the company's operations.
real_life.why: Verbs ('developed', 'improved') became nouns ('development', 'improvement'). The formal version sounds like a report — impersonal and compact. Nominalisation is exactly the move that turns everyday English into academic English.

reading.passage: The discovery of the vaccine marked a turning point. Its development took years of research and the cooperation of many nations. The reduction in deaths that followed was dramatic, and public confidence in science grew. However, the slow distribution of supplies caused frustration. In the end, the achievement reminded the world of the power of patience and persistence.

questions.answer: It makes the passage formal, compact and objective — the ideas (discovery, development, reduction) become the subjects.
